gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Bluetooth A2DP standard makes SBC the only codec every transmitter and every headphone must support (Bluetooth SIG, A2DP 1.4 §4.2.1). Better codecs are optional and work only when both ends share one. The FiiO DM13 sends aptX, aptX HD, aptX Low Latency and SBC but not AAC, so AirPods Pro 3 (AAC and SBC), soundcore Space One (SBC, AAC and LDAC) and Marshall Major V (SBC, AAC and LC3) all fall back to SBC. That is the only codec the Shanling EC Play transmits.
standout_why: I opened rottenwifi.com and macmyths.com, ranks 3 and 2, and theaudiotalk.com, rank 10. All three explain transmit versus receive, and ChatGPT's own answer does too. None of them mentions SBC, codec negotiation or what happens with AirPods. rottenwifi goes no further than saying 'Bluetooth 5.0 also does not, by itself, confirm support for AAC, aptX, low-latency audio.' macmyths stops at 'Do not infer codec support from the Bluetooth version.' theaudiotalk covers no codecs at all. av.com (rank 1) returned 403, so I could not check it.
decides: This confirms the plan works: any transmitting CD player will play through any A2DP headphone or speaker, because SBC is mandatory on both sides. It changes how to pick between the DM13 and the EC Play. The DM13's aptX HD only matters with headphones that also take aptX HD. With AirPods, soundcore Space One or Marshall Major V, both players send SBC, so that codec advantage disappears. The choice then comes down to battery (DM13 10 h rated, EC Play 12 h), skip protection and price. The EC Play's LDAC and AAC only work in its receive mode (phone to player), not when it sends CD audio.

findings.label: SBC is the one codec every A2DP device must support
findings.value: SBC mandatory for both source (encoder) and sink (decoder); all other codecs optional
findings.source_title: Bluetooth SIG, Advanced Audio Distribution Profile 1.4
findings.note: §4.2.1: 'A2DP mandates low complexity subband Coding (SBC). The device shall implement an SBC encoder when the device is the SRC' and 'an SBC decoder when the device is the SNK'. Table 4.1 marks SBC M and every other codec O.

findings.label: When a better codec gets used
findings.value: Only when both source and sink support the same codec
findings.source_title: Bluetooth SIG, Advanced Audio Distribution Profile 1.4
findings.note: §4.2.2: 'When both the SRC and the SNK support the same Optional codec interoperability requirements, these may be used.' §4.2.3 says the profile specifies nothing for vendor codecs such as aptX and LDAC. Falling back to SBC follows from SBC being mandatory on both ends; the spec does not use the word 'fallback'.

findings.label: Bluetooth transmit codecs
findings.value: aptX, aptX Low Latency, aptX HD, SBC (no AAC or LDAC listed)
findings.note: Quote: 'aptX, aptX Low Latency, aptX HD codecs as well as the standard SBC codec', on a 'Qualcomm Bluetooth platform'. Also: 'Standard version cannot transmit Bluetooth', so the shopper needs the BT version. 10 h rated battery from 3,750 mAh.

findings.label: Bluetooth transmit vs receive codecs
findings.value: Transmit SBC only; receive LDAC/AAC/SBC; Bluetooth 6.0
findings.note: Quote: 'Bluetooth Transmitter: SBC' and 'Bluetooth Receiver: LDAC/AAC/SBC'. Battery 3,450 mAh, up to 12 h. MSRP $199, with the note '(Check with dealers for USA pricing)'.
